name: file-sorter
desc: Free, open-source AI file organizer for Windows — sorts downloads by content, not extension, with undo. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Content-aware sorting** — a scanned invoice goes to Finance even though it is named scan_0042.pdf
✅ **Rule builder with preview** — lay out conditions and see where the current pile would land before starting
✅ **Watch folders** — the Downloads folder tidied minutes after files stop growing
✅ **Review queue** — low-confidence files wait for one-click confirmation instead of guessing
✅ **Undo journal** — one action reverts the last sorting run, file by file, paths restored
✅ **Tag sidecars** — optional tag files written next to documents for other tools to read
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, tiny classifier downloaded separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Free | Paid, Mac only | Free, endless
| Reads file content to decide | **Yes** | No | Partial | You do

faqQ: automatically organize my downloads folder by file content on Windows?
faqA: Rule tools match filenames, which fails the moment a bank statement is called download-34.pdf. file-sorter reads the content, proposes a destination, queues uncertain files for review and logs everything for one-click undo. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, and it never runs without a preview.
s1: Dark sorter (#121418, sky #0EA5E9): downloads pile with 42 files, proposed destination tags per item, Tidy button glowing, confidence note on three uncertain rows.
s2: Rule builder: condition row reading content contains invoice leads to Finance slash 2026, drag handles, live preview list of affected files.
s3: Undo journal: last run with 42 moves listed, per-file restore checkboxes, restore all button, timestamps and original paths in the table.
